results.title: 17 States Haven’t Had a Woman Governor, and 15 Haven’t Had a Woman Senator | Pew Research Center
results.content:
Overall, 53 women have held governorships in 33 states since 1925, when two women took the oath of office for the first time.

Nellie Tayloe Ross of Wyoming was nominated in and won a special election following the death of her husband, Gov. William Ross. Miriam “Ma” Ferguson of Texas, the first woman governor ever chosen in a general election, was sworn in just 15 days after her. [...] Ohio has technically had a female governor – Nancy Hollister, who served on an interim basis for less than two weeks after then-Gov. George Voinovich resigned on New Year’s Eve 1998 following his successful Senate campaign. But this year, Democrat Amy Acton could become the first _elected_ woman governor there. [...] Five current women governors are their state’s first: Democrats Janet Mills of Maine, Kathy Hochul of New York and Abigail Spanberger of Virginia; and Republicans Sarah Huckabee Sanders of Arkansas and Kim Reynolds of Iowa. Hochul and Sanders are seeking reelection this fall, while Mills (who is term-limited) and Reynolds (who is not seeking reelection) are departing.

results.title: Healey wins second term, defeating GOP challenger Mike Minogue | WBUR News
results.content:
The 55-year-old Arlington resident became Massachusetts’ first elected female governor and the country’s first openly lesbian governor, just hours ahead of Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek, who was also elected in 2022.

A civil rights lawyer who worked in the state attorney general’s office, Healey went on to head that office after winning the seat in 2014. She served for eight years as the state’s top law enforcement official before her run for governor. [...] The race also became defined by Healey’s nonstop anti-Trump talk. She sought to link Minogue, who donated nearly $1 million to Trump and other national Republicans in recent years — to the president, who is deeply unpopular in Massachusetts.

Healey won her first gubernatorial term in 2022, taking back the governor’s office for Democrats in one of the country’s bluest states after eight years of Republican Gov. Charlie Baker. She beat GOP nominee Geoff Diehl with 63.5% of the vote. [...] WBUR

results.title: First female governors in U.S. elected | November 4, 1924 | HISTORY
results.content:
On November 4, 1924, voters in Texas and Wyoming elect the nation’s first female governors: Miriam Amanda “Ma” Ferguson of Texas and Nellie Tayloe Ross of Wyoming. Both former first ladies of their states, the women enter the race in place of their husbands, though under vastly different circumstances. [...] Miriam Ferguson served two nonconsecutive terms as governor: 1925 to 1927 and 1933 to 1935. She ran for the office five times in total, losing her final bid in 1940 before retiring from public life. She died on June 25, 1961, at age 86. [...] From historical figures like Jeannette Rankin, the first woman in Congress, to modern ones like Tammy Duckworth, the first disabled person in Congress, meet 5 women who have paved the way for others in politics.

results.title: Record number of female governors elected
results.content:
Slide 1 of 1

In Maine, Hannah Pingree was projected to win the governor’s race, keeping a woman in the highest statewide office after Janet Mills’ two terms. In Massachusetts and New York, Maura Healey and Kathy Hochul were re-elected.

Several races — including those in Oregon and New Hampshire — remained uncalled after midnight ET. But those races also had two female major-party nominees competing. [...] Acton in Ohio, Hinojosa in Texas, Blackburn in Tennessee, Amy Klobuchar in Minnesota, Helena Foulkes in Rhode Island and Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia picked up governorships currently held by men.

Georgia voters led the historic night with an early victory for Bottoms, a former Atlanta mayor and adviser to former President Joe Biden, who will become the first Black female governor in U.S. history.

In her victory speech Tuesday night, Bottoms quoted the 1971 song “If I Were Your Woman.” [...] Voters in 15 states have elected female governors, setting a record in Tuesday’s election as Democrats made sweeping gains in races up and down the ballot.

With some governor’s races still unresolved, at least eight Democratic women were projected to win their contests, and two Republican women — Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders and Tennessee Gov.-elect Marsha Blackburn — were projected to do the same.

results.title: In historic night, voters elect first Black woman, first Black Republican as governors • Stateline
results.content:
For the first time ever, at least three Black governors will serve simultaneously in the United States, according to Tuesday’s unofficial results. Lance Bottoms and Donalds will join Maryland Gov. Wes Moore, a Democrat, who easily won reelection Tuesday.

Before Moore, only two other Black governors had ever been elected: Deval Patrick in Massachusetts and L. Douglas Wilder in Virginia, both Democrats.
